A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same Tru-POMDP work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.7 are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation experiments on 300 household rearrangement tasks, including baseline comparisons and component ablations in Figures 2–5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original simulation results, baseline comparisons, ablations, and illustrative execution in Appendix A.7.

M1.justification: The Tree of Hypotheses, hybrid belief update, dynamic action space, and belief-tree search remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 revises the generator prompt, but its displayed rollout code is identical, supporting a documentation correction rather than a changed deployed planner.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same rearrangement tasks across five RoboCasa kitchen layouts and three difficulty levels. Appendix A.4 retains the same task-generation pipeline; no additional domain or test scenario appears.

E2.justification: The five baseline identities remain unchanged, but Section 5.2 substantively revises the reported LLM-MCTS specification: a single maximum-likelihood goal/placement hypothesis becomes a closed-domain POMDP belief using known objects and object-location probability vectors. This changes the stated comparator formulation; the retained plots do not establish reimplementation or rerunning.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains 100 tasks per difficulty level, step limits of 25/30/35, the 600-second planning limit, GPT-4.1, and identical evaluation metrics. Appendix A.5 preserves the search and belief-generation hyperparameters.

E4.justification: The same five component ablations and their analyses remain in Section 5.3 and Figures 4–5. Appendix A.7 retains the same housewarming-task execution example; no new robustness, sensitivity, or error analysis is reported.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages with standard errors in Figures 2 and 4. No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Figures 2–5 contain identical result graphics, and the corresponding numerical statements and rankings are retained. Appendix A.7 also preserves the same execution trace and reported findings.

T1.justification: The POMDP definitions, Equations (1)–(6), particle-weight construction, and DESPOT discussion are unchanged. The new conditional-independence caveat explains the existing factorization and its limitations without adding a formal model, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The first contribution changes from being the first integration of LLM reasoning with principled household POMDP planning to being the first framework addressing open-ended POMDPs. This refines the novelty claim, while the abstract and principal performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly acknowledges conditional independence between object placements and the need for systematic factorization when dependencies are more complex. Section 5.2 also adds the applicability argument that LLM-MCTS cannot handle targets outside its closed object set.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 replaces an object-discovery prompt with rearrangement instructions specifying destination/object pairs, held-object access, and OPEN/PICK/PLACE actions, aligning the prompt with the existing code. Section 4.3 clarifies the rollout function's inputs and output. Hardware, hyperparameters, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The same 34 references remain, but Section 2.3 recharacterizes LLM-MCTS as using state distributions rather than a single hypothesis. The revised positioning distinguishes its closed-domain location uncertainty from Tru-POMDP's uncertainty over unknown objects and ambiguous goals.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify open-ended uncertainty, related-work distinctions, and rollout-policy generation. The revision also updates affiliation numbering, the conference footer, funding acknowledgments, and a broken figure reference. The overall section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from before Section 3.2 into Section 4.1, and appendix figures and tables reflow. Figure 7 now shares a page with its explanatory paragraph. Figure contents, chart legends, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 aligns the Appendix A.2 prompt with the existing rearrangement code, resolving a local reproducibility inconsistency. It also clarifies the distinction from LLM-MCTS and explicitly acknowledges the independence limitation. These focused improvements make the method and its scope easier to assess while retaining the original empirical evidence.
